Stepping into the Unknown: Joining a Ski Chalet Solo

For travellers who love winter sports but lack a dedicated ski companion, group operators offer a structured alternative to traveling entirely alone. A recent organized ski trip to Les Deux Alpes in the French Alps brought together 17 strangers in a single large chalet to navigate the slopes, share meals, and test the dynamics of group travel.

Participants joined for varied personal reasons: some were recovering from life changes or navigating relationships where partners did not ski, while others simply needed a break from family routines. Operating through specialist company Friendship Travel—which has run solo travel itineraries for more than two decades—the week-long package included chalet accommodation, travel arrangements, most meals, and organized group ski lessons.

On the Slopes and Around the Chalet

Group trips require participants to balance shared itineraries with personal independence. Guests were grouped by self-assessed skiing ability on the first morning, utilizing the resort's infrastructure, including the Jandri 3S cable car which accesses high-altitude terrain and views of the Écrins national park.

While structured skiing and après-ski gatherings at local venues helped forge camaraderie, group travel also presents everyday social logistics. Participants noted the minor etiquette navigation typical of shared chalets, from punctuality and seating arrangements to deciding when to break away for solo skiing.

Industry Context and Practical Considerations

According to Friendship Travel founder Colum McLornan, the perception of solo travel has shifted significantly since the company launched in 1999, moving away from past social stigmas toward a recognized, fast-growing sector focused on independence and personal flexibility.

For readers evaluating similar trips, here is a breakdown of verified details, uncertainties, and verification steps:

  • Confirmed Facts: The trip took place in Les Deux Alpes, France, utilizing a shared chalet hosted by Friendship Travel. The itinerary included daily ski lessons, shared dinners, and high-altitude skiing accessed via the Jandri 3S cable car.
  • What Remains Unknown: Individual budgeting variations outside the package, exact group demographics for future weeks, and personal interpersonal compatibility vary entirely by trip.
  • Practical Implications: Booking equipment hire in advance can yield savings (such as €40 noted by participants), and travellers can typically choose between private rooms or sharing with a same-sex peer to adjust costs.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review official itineraries, current pricing, and package inclusions directly through the [Guardian Travel Report](https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2026/oct/26/group-skiing-trip-solo-travellers-les-deux-alpes-france-alps) or by checking specialized solo operator platforms.
